area: Phase 5/6 enablement safety recon: shared pages, PageRegion globality, interaction cross-cuts, nav slot groups, slot accounting axes, per-route SEO cascade, and where authored.enablement belongs
findings: METHOD + HONESTY PREFACE. All numbers below are measured from artifacts on disk; I implemented nothing in src/ and ran no smoke suite (so no mutex was needed). Three derivations are mine, not repo APIs: (a) region membership for an arbitrary nodeId is NOT stored anywhere -- page-regions.json records only region ROOT nodeIds per (pageSourceId, viewport) -- so I rebuilt membership by walking each runtime page tree from its region roots (throwaway scratch script); (b) the interaction trigger/target graph is not a standalone artifact, it is data-wr-* props on the runtime IR, so I scanned those; (c) inbound-link counts per route I derived by joining slots.json url slots to slot-bindings.json pageIds. DISAGREEMENT I MUST REPORT: the stripe page-regions run on disk (data/stripe.com/page-regions/2026-08-26T16-14-08-675Z) was compiled from the OLDER template data/stripe.com/recon-templates/2026-08-18T10-45-40-007Z (9,529 slots), NOT from the newest template 2026-08-26T22-38-06-075Z (4,661 slots, route-policy.json applied). No region compile exists for the newest stripe template. Q1 route->pageSourceId numbers therefore come from the NEWEST template directly; all region numbers come from the 2026-08-18 lineage. The route->pageSourceId sharing is identical in all three stripe templates I checked, so Q1 transfers; region counts do not.

1a. PAGE SHARING -- LINEAR (accepted template data/linear.app/recon-templates/2026-08-25T21-53-26-980Z). 8 routes, 8 distinct pageSourceIds, 8 distinct pageFiles, ZERO many-to-one groups. renderCoverage: exact-observed x8. behaviorCoverage: exact-verified x8. Linear is the EASY case and must never be used to validate Phase 5 safety.

1b. PAGE SHARING -- STRIPE newest template (data/stripe.com/recon-templates/2026-08-26T22-38-06-075Z). 20 routes, 18 distinct pageSourceIds, 18 distinct pageFiles. EXACTLY TWO many-to-one groups, and the SAME JSON FILE is loaded for both members: pages/p000012.json <- {/resources/more/arr-loans-explained (representative:true, renderCoverage exact-observed, scope collection-representative, slotCount 433), /resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained (representative:true, renderCoverage family-represented, scope structure-only, slotCount 0)}; pages/p000013.json <- {/resources/more/kit-digital (exact-observed, structure-only, slotCount 0), /resources/more/what-is-carding-how-this-type-of-fraud-works-and-how-businesses-can-prevent-it (family-represented, structure-only, slotCount 0)}. ARTIFACT FIELDS THAT EXPRESS IT: site-map.json routes[].pageId (src/recon-template/site-map.ts:55 `pageId: route.pageSourceId`), routes[].familyId + routes[].representative + routes[].renderCoverage, and app/reconstruction-data/route-map.json routes[].pageSourceId + routes[].pageFile. A THIRD, COARSER grouping also exists and is bigger: familyId. f000012 has memberCount 4 and f000013 memberCount 3 -- routes /resources/more/how-can-my-customers-pay-by-bank-a-guide (p000016), /resources/more/how-to-launch-an-issuing-product-... (pageId x000001, an x-prefixed id, not p-prefixed) and /resources/more/uk-to-eu-vat-compliance (p000017) are family members with their OWN pageSourceIds. So family sharing != page sharing; only pageSourceId identity means physically-the-same tree.

1c. PAGE SHARING -- THE STRUCTURAL REASON THIS IS UNFIXABLE AT REGION GRANULARITY. src/regions/skeleton.ts:119-130 regionIdOf() namespaces a page-scoped region id by pageSourceId, NOT route, and the comment states why: 'routes -> pageSourceId is MANY-TO-ONE: keying on a route would mint N identical regions for one shared page and force an arbitrary choice of the route.' Consequence: `p000012:rgn:main1:section:3` is LITERALLY THE SAME ID for /resources/more/arr-loans-explained and /resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained. There is no region id at which 'disable this section for one route only' can even be expressed. src/regions/types.ts:158-163 RegionPageSchema carries `routes: z.array(z.string())` with the comment 'Many routes -> one pageSourceId. Never collapsed to the first one.' -- that array IS the blast radius and a Phase-5 UI must render it. MEASURED blast radius on stripe's compiled regions: 130 of 1014 region ids are reachable from more than one route; routes-per-region histogram {1: 884, 2: 128, 20: 2}; of the 130 multi-route regions, 128 are scope=page (the two shared-page groups, 64 page-scoped regions each) and 2 are scope=global. On linear the histogram is {1: 63, 8: 5} -- the 5 multi-route regions are exactly the 5 global ones.

1d. PAGE SHARING BLEEDS INTO THE SLOT LAYER TOO. On the newest stripe template, 4,511 of 4,661 slots carry a `route` field, and the routes represented are only 10 of the 20: /, /careers/apply/..., /careers/listing/..., /cookie-settings, /customers/hargreaves-lansdown, /en-hk/customers/amp, /industries/media-entertainment, /legal/becs, /newsroom/news/tour-berlin-2025, /resources/more/arr-loans-explained. The sibling route /resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained owns ZERO slots yet renders the same DOM. Root cause with citation: src/recon-template/grouping.ts:92-93 and :289-294 build `routeByPage` as 'pageId -> canonical route path (FIRST route serving that page)' -- a page slot's `route` names one route only. A Phase 5/6 surface that reads slot.route to decide scope will silently under-report the routes affected.

2a. PAGEREGION SHAPE. Definition and schema: src/regions/types.ts. A region is a (landmark scope, child path) address inside ONE viewport tree, promoted to global when the strict lift fires. regionId = `<scopeKey>:rgn:<landmarkKey>:<childPath>` (skeleton.ts:128); scopeKey is 'global' or the owning pageSourceId; landmarkKey is kind+document-order ordinal (nav1, main1, footer1, doc); childPath is `div:1>section:3` (1-based nth-of-same-tag) or `self`. STABILITY: the id survives markup edits INSIDE the region (the structural hash exists precisely to announce those, types.ts:175-181) but does NOT survive an insert ABOVE it that shifts an nth-of-type index, nor a change to REGION_COMPILER_VERSION (types.ts:40, 'Bumped whenever the SELECTION POLICY changes, because the ids then move'). ROOT NODE: RegionOccurrence.nodeId is the region root's `data-wr-node` value (types.ts:139-141: 'The join key, not the id'), one occurrence per viewport; desktop and mobile are independent trees and a mobile root whose TAG disagrees is kept apart under a @mobile id. JOIN TO slot-bindings.json: purely `(pageId, viewport, nodeId)` -- compile.ts:23-31 and :225-244 walk the region subtree's node ids and pull bindingsByNode; no DOM attribute is added (types.ts:20-25 forbids it), which is consistent with the DO-NOT-TOUCH rule against data-wr-slot.

2b. REGION SLOT-COUNT DISTRIBUTION (measured). LINEAR (68 regions): slotKeys per region min 0, p25 3, median 12, p75 60, p90 84, max 1007; 4 zero-slot regions; sum 3,736 slotKey memberships over 3,079 distinct slots. Landmark kinds: main 53, footer 8, document 4, nav 3. STRIPE-2026-08-18 (1014 regions): min 0, p25 0, median 4, p75 9, p90 23, max 464; 265 ZERO-SLOT regions. Landmark kinds: header 449, nav 267, document 214, aside 42, main 39, footer 3. Granularity is wildly non-uniform (this is already recorded honestly in region-plan.ts:32-33) -- a Phase-5 UI that lists 'regions' flat will show an operator 265 stripe regions that contain no editable content at all.

2c. SLOTS ARE SHARED ACROSS REGIONS -- the fact that actually governs safety. On linear, 134 of 3,079 distinct slotKeys belong to more than one region; regions-per-slotKey histogram {1: 2945, 2: 41, 3: 1, 4: 6, 5: 2, 8: 84}. The 84 keys at multiplicity 8 are the FOOTER: all eight page-scoped footer regions carry an IDENTICAL 84-key set, all prefixed `global.footer.` (e.g. global.footer.link.about.href/.label). Slots.json scope tally: global 131, page 2,948 -- and 131 = 84 footer + 47 header-nav exactly. So the SLOT layer already knows linear's footer is global even though the REGION compiler does not.

2d. WHICH REGIONS ARE GLOBAL -- CONFIRMING/CORRECTING TASK 27. Strict rule (compile.ts:267-294): identical landmarkKey AND childPath AND rootTag AND subtree structuralHash on EVERY non-locale page, with at least globalMinPages=2 such pages; locale-prefixed-only pages are excluded from the denominator (compile.ts:103-112). LINEAR RESULT: 5 global regions -- global:rgn:nav1:self (nav, 39 elements, 528 bindings, 47 slots, 8 pages, 224 dynamic-template bindings), global:rgn:doc:div:1>div:1>a:1 (32 slots) and three zero-slot spans. counts.nearGlobalGroups=1, nearGlobalMaxPages=7, globalCandidatesLandmarkQualifiedOnly=0. TASK 27's CLAIM CONFIRMED IN SUBSTANCE, CORRECTED IN DETAIL: the footer is missed, but 'shared by 7 of 8 pages' is only true of the HASH. Measured: all 8 pages carry footer1|self as a <footer> at the same path; 7 of 8 hash 9bee49417039 (110 elements) and /changelog (p000002) hashes 0de8a85e0f5e (117 elements); all 8 carry the SAME 84 global-scope slot keys. So by landmark+path it is 8/8, by slot set it is 8/8, and only by structural hash is it 7/8. The single element-count delta on /changelog is what costs linear its footer. STRIPE RESULT is far worse: only 2 global regions out of 1014, while counts.nearGlobalGroups=72, nearGlobalMaxPages=10, globalCandidatesLandmarkQualifiedOnly=17. Alternative-signature coverage measured by me: on stripe, landmarkKey+childPath yields 210 groups of which 88 span >=2 pages and 66 span >=half the pages; structuralHash yields 156 groups of which 72 span >=2 pages. And 127 page-scoped stripe region ids hold at least one global-scope slot (45 of them hold ONLY global-scope slots), e.g. rgn:nav6:div:2>section:1 recurring on 9 pages with 48 global slots each, rgn:header1:div:2>div:3>div:1>h1:1 recurring on 10 pages, rgn:footer1:self recurring on 3 pages with 149 global slots. On linear the same measure gives 9 regions holding global slots, of which 8 are page-scoped (the footers).

2e. HOW A BUILDER SHOULD DECIDE 'THIS REGION IS GLOBAL' (my answer, from the numbers above). Do NOT use region.scope=='global' -- it is the strict lift and it under-reports by 8 regions on linear and by ~125 on stripe. Use a THREE-SIGNAL union and treat ANY hit as global-for-enablement-purposes: (i) region.scope=='global'; (ii) region.slotKeys contains at least one slot whose slots.json scope=='global' -- this alone recovers linear's footer exactly and 127 stripe regions, and it is authoritative because the slot compiler already ran the cross-page identity analysis; (iii) the region's (landmark.key, childPath) signature occurs on >= 2 distinct pageSourceIds regardless of structuralHash -- 12 groups on linear, 88 on stripe. Signal (ii) is the cheapest and highest-precision and should be the primary; (iii) is the catch-all for zero-slot chrome. Do NOT relax REGION_POLICY or the compiler itself: the artifact is a versioned frozen sibling and changing globalMinPages or the hash requirement moves every id.

3a. INTERACTION GRAPH -- WHERE IT LIVES. There is no interaction graph artifact in the template. The SiteSpec compile (src/sitespec/types.ts:1392-1420 CompiledPatternSchema, :1272-1370 CompiledObservedTargetSchema, :1240-1270 CompiledTargetSchema) is upstream and is NOT copied into the recon-template run. What survives into the template is DOM props on the runtime IR, emitted by src/reconstruction/interaction-bindings.ts:718-815 bindingProps() and src/reconstruction/compile-node.ts:427-450, and read by app/src/runtime/InteractionRuntime.tsx. Trigger identity = an element carrying `data-wr-op` (plus data-wr-pattern, data-wr-pattern-id, data-wr-mechanism, data-wr-field/from/to). Target identity comes through THREE channels: (1) `data-wr-target-node` = the target's SiteSpec nodeId, the only channel that is directly region-joinable (compile-node.ts:435 also emits `data-wr-target-id`, the generated DOM id `wr-<pageId>-<viewport>-<nodeId>`); (2) `data-wr-obs` = a JSON array of observed targets with compact keys, where `i` is a generated DOM id of an EXISTING node, `hn` is the mountHostNodeId a newly-mounted branch attaches under, `x` the child index, `tpl` the captured template (interaction-bindings.ts:770-812); (3) `data-wr-dyn-id`/`data-wr-dyn-template` = a region the runtime MOUNTS, whose nodes carry data-wr-dyn-node only INSIDE the serialized template string (185 occurrences inside p000001.json payloads on linear) and therefore have NO region membership until mount -- their bindings deliberately join to the HOST node's region (compile.ts:41-46).

3b. INTERACTION GRAPH -- MEASURED CROSS-REGION CUTS ON LINEAR. Attribute census over all 8 pages x 2 viewports (18,918 elements, 17,337 with data-wr-node): data-wr-op 23, data-wr-target-node 2, data-wr-target-id 2, data-wr-obs 15, data-wr-dyn-template 16, data-wr-unknown 11 (inert, flagged), data-wr-reveal 11, data-wr-hidden 68. Resolving all three target channels: 23 triggers, all 23 inside some region, producing 23 target edges -- 6 SAME-REGION, 3 CROSS-REGION (3 distinct region pairs), 14 pointing at a node OUTSIDE EVERY REGION (portal/document-root mounts), 0 unresolved. On stripe-2026-08-18: 27 triggers, 59 edges -- 12 same-region, 8 cross-region (5 distinct pairs), 39 outside-every-region. The 'outside every region' bucket is a SECOND hazard class Phase 5 must name and is the LARGER one on both sites: the mount host is usually n000002, the adapted document root, which no region owns, so a mounted mega-menu has no region to be disabled with and no region to protect it.

3c. INTERACTION GRAPH -- THE THREE REAL LINEAR CROSS-REGION EXAMPLES (all on p000001 = route /, viewport desktop; all three converge on ONE target node). (1) trigger n000021, <button>, pattern disclosure, in GLOBAL region `global:rgn:nav1:self` -> target n001530 (<span>, DOM id wr-p000001-desktop-n001530) in PAGE region `p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:3`, via data-wr-obs entry {k:'existing-visibility', d:'disappeared', i:'wr-p000001-desktop-n001530'}. (2) trigger n000128, <button>, disclosure, in `p000001:rgn:nav2:self` -> the same n001530 in `p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:3`. (3) trigger n001659, <button>, disclosure, in `p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:4` -> the same n001530 in `p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:3`, via {k:'existing-visibility', d:'appeared', dsp:'block'}. So disabling the single page region `p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:3` on the homepage silently breaks three verified interactions, one of which is triggered from the GLOBAL header that renders on all 8 routes. Additionally: 224 of linear's 262 dynamic-template bindings live in the ONE region global:rgn:nav1:self, so disabling that region on any single route removes a 224-binding mega-menu from all 8 routes; the only other dyn host is p000006:rgn:main1:div:2>section:1>div:1 (38 bindings). On stripe the largest dyn hosts are p000001/p000002/p000003:rgn:footer1:self at 559/554/554 bindings.

4a. NAVIGATION SLOT GROUPS -- THE REAL MECHANISM. There IS a groupId. src/recon-template/types.ts:316-321: `groupId: z.string().optional()` with the comment 'Related slots (e.g. a CTA's label + href) share a groupId', alongside role, type ('text'|'url'|'image'), scope, editability, urlKind ('internal'|'external'|'hash') and defaultValue. Example: slot sl000001 key `global.header.nav.homepage.href`, role navigation.href, type url, scope global, groupId `global.header.nav.homepage`, urlKind internal, defaultValue '/homepage', bindingIds b000001..b000016 (16 bindings = 8 pages x 2 viewports).

4b. NAVIGATION SLOT GROUPS -- MEASURED ON LINEAR. 3,079 slots; 1,553 carry a groupId across 635 distinct groups; group-size histogram {1:194, 2:272, 3:14, 4:36, 5:97, 6:18, 9:4}. EVERY url slot is grouped (0 url slots without a groupId); 1,526 text slots are ungrouped. 443 groups contain a url slot, and 439 of those are a true href+label pair (4 href-only, 0 label-only). Role tally over all slots: link.label 842, link.href 385, cta.label 41, cta.href 39, navigation.label 36, navigation.href 19, plus content.text 1463, image.content 195, heading.secondary 42, hero.headline 7, footer.text 6, hero.description 3, heading.primary 1. NAVIGATION-LIKE by role: 19 navigation groups + 39 cta groups + 385 link groups = 443 link-bearing groups; by scope 56 are global-scope and 387 page-scope. urlKind split of the 443: internal 283, hash 106, external 54.

4c. NAVIGATION SLOT GROUPS -- WHAT PHASE 6 CAN AND CANNOT AUTO-REMOVE (linear, measured). Of the 443 link-bearing groups, only 26 point at one of the 8 template routes; 257 point at internal paths that are NOT template routes (178 distinct targets: /homepage, /now, /contact, /docs, /login, /signup, /agents, /asks, ...); 54 external; 106 hash. Of the 26 route-targeting groups, 12 are GLOBAL-scope. INBOUND LINK COUNT PER ROUTE (url slots -> bindings -> source pages): / = 1 slot / 16 bindings / 8 source pages; /changelog = 4 slots / 28 bindings / 8 pages; /customers = 10 / 48 / 8; /customers/automattic = 3 / 6 / 2 pages (p000003, p000006 only); /integrations = 2 / 24 / 8; /plan = 3 / 26 / 8; /pricing = 2 / 32 / 8; /security = 1 / 16 / 8. READ: disabling any route except /customers/automattic requires editing a link that renders on ALL EIGHT pages, most of it through global-scope header/footer slots. Auto-removable deterministically: the 26 route-targeting groups (the href AND its paired label, because 439/443 are pairs and the groupId gives you the label for free). NOT auto-removable, must become a requirement: the 257 internal-off-template groups -- the site links to 194 internal paths (site-map.json internalLinks) but only 8 are reconstructed, so Phase 6 cannot tell an intentionally-dangling link from a newly-broken one without the served-output check in src/seo/link-qa.ts (brokenInternal classification).

5a. SLOT ACCOUNTING AXES -- EXACT ENUMS, QUOTED. src/content-injection/types.ts:981-999: `export const SLOT_ORIGINS = ['user-provided','derived-copy','generated-marketing','synthetic-fact','source-preserved'] as const;` and `export const SLOT_DISPOSITIONS = ['applied','preserved','removed','human-required','unresolved'] as const;`. The header comment (types.ts:962-980) states they are deliberately orthogonal: 'ORIGIN answers where did the value that renders here come from. DISPOSITION answers what happened to this slot in this run... One mixed enum cannot express that without losing information.' SlotAccountingEntry (types.ts:1000-1021) requires EXACTLY ONE of each plus scope, optional route, type, editability, customerFacing and detail, and SlotAccountingFile carries a `reconciliation` block proving every in-scope slot appears exactly once and both axis totals equal the in-scope count.

5b. SLOT ACCOUNTING -- THERE IS A `removed` VALUE BUT IT DOES NOT MEAN 'NOT RENDERED'. src/content-injection/accounting.ts:105-110 is the ONLY producer of it: `if (isEmptyValue(value)) { return { origin, disposition: 'removed', detail: 'value written as empty -- the content was removed on purpose' }; }`. That is an EMPTY VALUE IN A STILL-RENDERED NODE. Nothing anywhere in src/ produces or consumes a 'not rendered' disposition -- I grepped. CONCLUSION FOR THE BUILDER: Phase 5/6 MUST add explicit new disposition values (my proposal: `disabled-region` and `disabled-route`) rather than reusing `removed`, and must extend the reconciliation so a disabled slot is still counted in the in-scope denominator. Reusing `removed` would make an intentionally emptied headline and a physically deleted section indistinguishable in the one artifact whose whole purpose is that they are distinguishable. Note SLOT_DISPOSITIONS is a `z.enum` restated inside SlotAccountingFile.dispositionValues, so adding a value is a schema-visible, diff-visible change -- good.

5c. SLOT ACCOUNTING -- WHAT COUNTS AS CUSTOMER-FACING. accounting.ts:163 `customerFacing: slot.editability === 'editable' ? 'confirmed' : 'ambiguous'`, and types.ts:1011-1018 states the rule: 'confirmed only where the template compiler was confident the slot is customer-facing (editability=editable). A review slot is ambiguous and is counted in its own bucket, never folded into a success number.' On linear that is 1,586 editable / 1,493 review out of 3,079. There is a THIRD, invisible population named in SlotAccountingFile.scopeHonesty.templateExcludedCandidates -- linear manifest.counts.excludedCandidates = 1,435 candidates the template compiler suppressed entirely. Phase 5/6 must not let a disabled region shrink the denominator; it must move slots between disposition buckets only.

6. SEO SURFACES PER ROUTE -- THE COMPLETE LIST OF CODE SITES A PHASE-6 CASCADE MUST TOUCH. The route table is app/reconstruction-data/route-map.json and it is the single source of truth for everything below. (1) src/seo/production-plan.ts:44-64 loadTemplateForSeo() reads route-map.json into TemplateRoute[]. (2) src/seo/production-plan.ts:172 `const routes: ProductionRouteSeo[] = template.routes.map((route) => {...})` -- THE route loop; inside it, :175-198 title + description (needs-input when the route is outside contentRun.scopedRoutes), :200-202 robotsMeta, :223-231 canonical (`${origin}${route.path}`, self-referential), :232-248 openGraph {title, description, type, locale, url, image, siteName}, :249-254 twitter, :255 jsonLd. (3) src/seo/robots-sitemap.ts:58-62 -- the sitemap urlset is `for (const route of plan.routes) lines.push('<url><loc>' + origin + route.path + '</loc></url>')`; same module emits robots.txt. (4) src/seo/render-head.ts:34 renderRouteHead / :66 renderPlanHead -- the per-route <head> block. (5) src/production/bake.ts:107-117 bakeRouteTitles writes plan titles back INTO route-map.json (so the title lands in both the head and the RSC flight payload). (6) src/production/bake.ts:119-133 convertToStaticExport -- the route table decides which static files Next emits. (7) src/production/bake.ts:172-174 routeHtmlFile() and :221-244 the per-route head splice (a plan route with no exported file is a headSpliceFailure). (8) src/production/bake.ts:297-315 the per-route source-brand census. (9) src/production/run.ts:470-472 copies sitemap.xml into the SERVED output in indexable mode (in preview it stays a package-only sitemap.preview.xml, bake.ts:345-358). (10) src/production/qa.ts:355-395 per-route http/title-served/head-block/robots-meta checks + the /sitemap.xml 200-vs-404 check; :406 a second per-route loop. (11) src/seo/link-qa.ts:36-45 auditAnchors classifies every anchor against the route-key set -- this is the ONLY place that can prove a disabled route left no broken internal link, and it is therefore the honest clearing condition for a Phase-6 requirement. (12) src/release/collect.ts:257 (`const routes = templateManifest.routes`), :297-330 (the `content-route` requirement, one per uninjected route), :341-393 (og-image / twitter.site per route), :396-412 (organization-logo from jsonLd omissions), :646-660 routeReadiness. (13) the served app itself: app/[[...slug]]/page.tsx findRoute() -> notFound() for anything outside the table. A disabled route that is removed from route-map.json disappears from 1,3,5,6,7,9,10,13 automatically; 2,4,8,11,12 need explicit handling.

7a. WHERE ENABLEMENT SHOULD LIVE -- THE SUBSTRATE CONSTRAINTS. AuthoredStateSchema (src/release/types.ts:360-386) is `.strict()` with required slotValues/theme/updatedAt and OPTIONAL, ABSENT-WHEN-EMPTY assets and brand. The comment at :365-374 gives the binding reason: hashAuthoredState (revisions.ts:121-123) hashes the snapshot as captured, so a required-but-empty map would change the hash of every historical authored state and manufacture a spurious revision on the next prepare, and every release-project.json already on disk lacks the field. THEREFORE enablement must be added the same way and must be TWO separate optional fields, not one: `authored.disabledRoutes?: Record<string, {...}>` and `authored.disabledRegions?: Record<string, {...}>`, each deleted entirely when its last entry goes (the removeAuthoredAsset round-trip pattern, authored.ts:189-203). Both must also be added to graph.ts AUTHORED_FIELD_IMPACTS (:80-85), to freshness.ts resolutionSliceFor (:225-283), and to the revisions change summary, or an enablement edit will be invisible to release:plan.

7b. WHERE ENABLEMENT SHOULD LIVE -- WHICH STAGES MUST GO STALE, DERIVED FROM WHAT EACH STAGE ACTUALLY CONSUMES. STAGE_DEPENDENCIES (graph.ts:27-39): template<-reconstruction; content<-template; theme<-{template,content}; seo<-{template,content}; assets<-template; production<-{template,content,theme,seo,assets}. DISABLED ROUTE must directly stale content + seo + assets, and the DAG closure adds theme + production, i.e. everything except the frozen roots. Reasons, each from a real consumer: content -- contentStageRunner (stages.ts:102-115) computes `routes` from baseManifest.scopedRoutes and passes it to prepareContentRun, and a disabled route must leave that scope, which changes content-units, the region plan and slot accounting; seo -- seoStageRunner (stages.ts:276-300) rebuilds the plan from route-map + contentRun scopedRoutes and production-plan.ts:172 loops the route table, so title/description/canonical/og/twitter/jsonLd AND the sitemap urlset all move; assets -- assets/inventory.ts joins by slotKey and pageId (usageCount = pageIds.length at :386-387), so dropping a route can genuinely drop an asset requirement, and the count MUST be recomputed rather than assumed; theme -- theme depends on content in the graph and themeStageRunner pins its content run, so it staleness-cascades whether or not tokens move; production -- the bake, static export, head splice, brand census and QA are all per-route. DISABLED REGION must directly stale content + assets, closure adding theme + seo + production. Reasons: content -- the region's slotKeys leave the writable population and gain a new disposition; assets -- image slots inside a disabled region stop being referenced; seo -- indirectly, because production-plan derives description from pagePlan.primaryMessage which comes from the content run, AND because a disabled hero can remove the only source of a route's message; production -- the bake is where the region is physically not rendered. NOTE ON THE `brand` PRECEDENT (graph.ts:63-73): the authors deliberately chose OVER-staleness ('over-staleness costs a rebuild; under-staleness ships a decision the operator believes was applied'). Enablement should inherit that posture. AUTHORITATIVE MECHANISM: computeStageInputsHash (freshness.ts:285-303) over resolutionSliceFor is the real answer; authoredInvalidatedStages (graph.ts:155-180) is only a PREDICTION for the operator surface, and both must be updated together or release:plan and release:build will disagree -- exactly the class of drift the comment at graph.ts:117-124 records as already having happened once with routeContent.

7c. WHERE ENABLEMENT SHOULD LIVE -- TWO PLUMBING GAPS THE BUILDER WILL HIT IMMEDIATELY. (i) THE PAGEREGION ARTIFACT IS NOT IN THE RELEASE PROJECT AT ALL. I grepped src/release/ and src/production/ for page-regions / pageRegions: zero hits. The only entry point is the OPTIONAL `--regions-file` flag on src/cli-content-prepare.ts:36,80,142 -> packet.ts:71,344-359, and contentStageRunner (stages.ts:109) calls prepareContentRun WITHOUT it. Consequence, verified: `find data -name region-plan.json` returns NOTHING -- no region plan has ever been produced by a real run anywhere in data/. Phase 5 must first make page-regions.json a first-class release-project auxiliary (alongside auxiliary.seoSourceSnapshotDir) and pass it through contentStageRunner, or every enablement edit will reference regionIds that no build artifact knows about. Note freshness.ts:100 already lists region-plan.json among the content-stage inputs that stay INSIDE the hash, so the wiring is anticipated. (ii) THE EXISTING REGION CONSUMER LOSES SHARED-REGION INFORMATION. region-plan.ts:113-116 builds `regionBySlotKey` with FIRST-REGION-WINS (`if (!regionBySlotKey.has(key)) regionBySlotKey.set(key, region)`), so on linear all 84 footer slot keys map to p000001's footer region alone and the other 7 footer regions get no units. Any Phase-5 code that reuses that map to answer 'which regions own this slot' will under-report by 7x on linear. The GOOD news is region-plan.ts:82 already does the right thing for routes: `routes: [...new Set(region.pages.flatMap((page) => page.routes))].sort()` -- RegionContract.routes is the full, uncollapsed blast radius and is the field a safety check should read.

options.name: A. Page-identity gate (refuse per-route region disable on any shared page)
options.howItWorks: Before writing authored.disabledRegions[regionId], resolve the region's pageSourceIds, then resolve every route reaching each of them from site-map.json / route-map.json. If that route set is larger than the routes the operator selected, REFUSE the edit and surface the full list, offering only 'disable on all N routes' or 'cancel'. Region scope is left alone; nothing in src/regions changes.
options.measured: Would fire on 130 of 1014 stripe region ids (128 page-scoped, from the two shared-page groups p000012/p000013; 2 global spanning all 20 routes) and on 5 of 68 linear region ids (the 5 global ones). It would NOT fire on linear's 8 footer regions, because each footer region is page-scoped to exactly one route -- i.e. this option alone misses the 84 shared global.footer.* slots entirely.
options.cost: Cheapest option. Pure read of two artifacts already in the template; no schema change to page-regions.json; no new compile.
options.risk: Incomplete by construction. It catches PAGE sharing and misses SLOT sharing, which is the larger population: 134 shared slotKeys on linear, 127 stripe regions holding global-scope slots. An operator deleting linear's footer 'on /pricing' would sail through and then find /pricing's 84 footer slots still owned by 7 other regions whose values are the same keys.

options.name: B. Global-slot gate (refuse or cascade when a region owns global-scope slots)
options.howItWorks: Join region.slotKeys to slots.json scope. If any member slot has scope=='global', treat the region as global regardless of region.scope: the disable is site-wide or it is refused. Optionally split further: all-slots-global => pure chrome, offer site-wide disable; mixed => refuse and require the operator to pick individual slots instead.
options.measured: Fires on 9 of 68 linear regions (global:rgn:nav1:self with 47 global slots, plus all 8 footer regions with 84 global slots each) -- it recovers linear's footer exactly, which is the case Task 27 named. On stripe it fires on 127 of 1014 regions, 45 of which hold ONLY global slots (e.g. rgn:nav6:div:2>section:1 on 9 pages x 48 global slots, rgn:footer1:self x3 pages x 149 global slots).
options.cost: One extra artifact read (slots.json, already loaded by every content consumer) and one map. No compile change, no id change.
options.risk: Says nothing about page sharing: stripe's 128 shared page-scoped regions on p000012/p000013 mostly hold no global slots, so B alone lets an operator delete a section 'on /resources/more/arr-loans-explained' and silently delete it from /resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained too. B and A are complements, not alternatives.

options.name: C. Relax the region compiler's global lift (landmark+path instead of landmark+path+hash)
options.howItWorks: Change REGION_POLICY / the lift in src/regions/compile.ts:267-294 so a group lifts to global on identical landmarkKey + childPath + rootTag across every non-locale page, treating a differing structuralHash as drift to report rather than as a bar to promotion. The footer then gets ONE id and 'disable' is unambiguously site-wide.
options.measured: On linear this lifts footer1|self (8/8 pages by path, 2 distinct hashes: 9bee49417039 x7 at 110 elements, 0de8a85e0f5e on /changelog at 117) taking globals from 5 to 6 and collapsing 8 footer ids into 1. On stripe it would lift only 2 more (landmarkKey+childPath spans all 18 pages for just 2 groups), leaving 66 groups that span >=half the pages still page-scoped -- so it barely helps the hard site.
options.cost: REGION_COMPILER_VERSION must bump (types.ts:40 says so explicitly), which MOVES EVERY REGION ID. Every page-regions artifact on disk is invalidated and any stored enablement referencing an old id breaks.
options.risk: Highest. Task 28's contract freezes reconstruction semantics and treats page-regions as a versioned sibling with a small stable contract; region-plan.ts:26-33 explicitly promises the compiler's internals can change WITHOUT touching Content V2, but that promise runs the other way -- it does not license breaking ids under a live consumer. It also buys almost nothing on stripe. I recommend against.

options.name: D. Cascade instead of refuse (auto-expand the edit to its full blast radius, with a preview)
options.howItWorks: Never refuse. Compute the transitive closure of the edit -- every route reaching the region's pages, every other region sharing its global slots, every interaction whose trigger or target crosses the cut -- present it as a diff the operator confirms, then write ONE authored entry recording the closure as chosen. The closure is stored so a later re-render can prove what was agreed.
options.measured: Closure sizes measured: linear footer disable => 8 routes, 8 region ids, 84 slot keys. Linear global nav disable => 8 routes, 47 slots, 224 of the site's 262 dynamic-template bindings. Linear p000001:rgn:main1:div:2>section:3 disable => 3 verified interactions broken, 2 of them triggered from outside the region (n000021 in global:rgn:nav1:self, n000128 in p000001:rgn:nav2:self). Stripe /resources/more/arr-loans-explained region disable => 2 routes, 64 page-scoped region ids affected.
options.cost: Most implementation work: needs the interaction scan (three attribute channels), the slot-sharing map and the page->routes map, plus a UI that can render a closure honestly.
options.risk: A closure computed from data-wr-obs is only as complete as the observation was: 14 of linear's 23 target edges and 39 of stripe's 59 point at nodes OUTSIDE every region (usually n000002, the adapted document root), so the closure will contain 'unknown-region target' entries that cannot be resolved. Presenting those as safe would be dishonest; they must be shown as unresolved and must block, not decorate.

options.name: E. Refuse the cut, keep the region (visibility-only disable at the bake)
options.howItWorks: Do not remove the subtree. Mark it non-rendered at the production bake only, keeping node ids, interaction attributes and the slot join intact, and record a new disposition on its slots. Cross-region triggers keep resolving; a later re-enable is exact.
options.measured: Would leave all 23 linear / 27 stripe triggers resolvable and preserve the 262 / 1921 dynamic-template bindings' host joins. But it leaves the disabled content in the shipped bytes, which collides with the measured brand posture: bake.ts:297-315 runs a source-brand census over the FINAL exported route HTML, and a hidden-but-present section still counts there.
options.cost: Low engine cost, but it needs a real bake-time mechanism and a QA check that the region is genuinely absent from user-visible output.
options.risk: Dishonest by default: an operator who said 'delete this section' would ship it. It also cannot satisfy a Phase-6 requirement that a disabled route disappear from the sitemap, so it does not generalise from regions to routes.

recommendation: Adopt B + A + D together as ONE rule, and reject C and E. Concretely, the rule I recommend the builder implement is: (1) A region's ENABLEMENT SCOPE is not region.scope. Compute it as the union of three signals and take the widest: region.scope=='global'; OR any member slotKey has slots.json scope=='global'; OR the region's (landmark.key, childPath) signature occurs on >= 2 distinct pageSourceIds. Measured coverage of that union: linear 9 regions (recovers the footer that the strict lift misses -- 8/8 pages by path and by slot set, 7/8 only by hash), stripe 127+ regions. (2) A region's ROUTE BLAST RADIUS is RegionContract.routes -- the already-correct `[...new Set(region.pages.flatMap(p => p.routes))]` at region-plan.ts:82 -- never slot.route (first-route-only, grouping.ts:289-294) and never the regionId (pageSourceId-namespaced, skeleton.ts:128, so it cannot even name a route). If that radius is wider than the operator's selection, the edit is CASCADED with an explicit confirmation, not silently applied and not silently refused. (3) A cut is REFUSED, never cascaded, when it would break an interaction whose other end cannot be proven safe: scan data-wr-target-node, data-wr-obs[].i and data-wr-obs[].hn, and refuse when the counterpart resolves into a region that stays enabled (3 such edges on linear, 8 on stripe) or resolves to no region at all (14 on linear, 39 on stripe -- the larger bucket, and the one that must block rather than be waved through). (4) Store enablement as TWO optional, absent-when-empty authored fields -- authored.disabledRoutes and authored.disabledRegions -- following the assets/brand precedent exactly (types.ts:365-382, revisions.ts:121-123), and register both in AUTHORED_FIELD_IMPACTS and resolutionSliceFor in the same commit. Route disable stales content+seo+assets (closure: everything but the frozen roots); region disable stales content+assets (closure adds theme+seo+production). (5) Add TWO new SlotDisposition values, `disabled-region` and `disabled-route`; do NOT reuse `removed`, which accounting.ts:105-110 defines as an empty value in a still-rendered node. Keep the in-scope denominator unchanged so the reconciliation block still proves totals. (6) Phase 6 may auto-remove only the 26 linear slot groups (href+its paired label via groupId) that target a template route; the 257 internal-off-template groups become a requirement, and the clearing condition is src/seo/link-qa.ts reporting zero brokenInternal on the served candidate -- never the presence of an operator's request. (7) BLOCKING PREREQUISITE: page-regions.json is not wired into the release project at all (zero references in src/release and src/production; `find data -name region-plan.json` returns nothing, so no region plan has ever been produced by a real run). Make it a first-class release-project auxiliary and pass it through contentStageRunner before any of the above can be tested on real data.
risks: The stripe region measurements are from a template (2026-08-18T10-45-40-007Z, 9,529 slots, 1014 regions) that is NOT the newest stripe template (2026-08-26T22-38-06-075Z, 4,661 slots, route-policy.json applied). No page-regions compile exists for the newest one. Route->pageSourceId sharing is identical across all three, so Q1 transfers; the 1014-region / 127-global-slot-holder / 130-multi-route numbers do NOT, and would need a fresh compile to restate. I did not run one (it would write a new run directory).

Region membership for an arbitrary nodeId is not persisted anywhere. My cross-region interaction counts (linear 23 triggers / 6 same / 3 cross / 14 region-less; stripe 27 triggers / 12 same / 8 cross / 39 region-less) come from a throwaway script that re-derives membership by walking the runtime tree from the region roots in page-regions.json. The derivation is straightforward but it is MINE, not a repo function, and a builder should reimplement and re-measure rather than trust these figures.

The 'outside every region' target bucket is the largest hazard class on both sites and I cannot fully characterise it. Most of those edges point at n000002, the adapted document root. Portal-mounted content therefore has NO region to be disabled with and NO region protecting it, and data-wr-dyn-node exists only inside serialized data-wr-dyn-template strings (185 occurrences inside p000001.json on linear), so mounted nodes have no static region membership at all. Any Phase-5 safety rule that reasons only about region-to-region edges is blind here.

region-plan.ts:113-116 maps a slotKey to its FIRST owning region. On linear that collapses 8 footer regions into 1 for all 84 global.footer.* keys. Reusing that map for a safety check would under-report the affected region set by 7x. The correct map is many-to-many and must be built fresh.

Disabling a route legitimately removes SEO surfaces, and that is precisely the shape of the honesty failure a verifier already caught in Phase 2. A requirement (content-route, og-image, seo-fact, organization-logo -- collect.ts:297-412) must NOT clear because a route was marked disabled. It clears only when the produced output proves it: the route absent from route-map.json AND from plan.routes AND from the sitemap urlset AND from the exported HTML set AND link-qa reporting zero brokenInternal pointing at it. Building the disable so that it merely filters the requirement collector would reproduce the exact defect the program was corrected for.

authored.enablement changes the meaning of every count downstream (slots in scope, asset usageCount = pageIds.length at inventory.ts:386, requirement totals, the 22-suite / 2472-check baseline). Under-staleness here ships a site the operator believes was edited. The brand precedent (graph.ts:63-73) chose over-staleness deliberately; enablement should too, and the graph.ts prediction and freshness.ts authoritative hash must be updated in the same commit or release:plan and release:build will disagree -- the drift already recorded at graph.ts:117-124.

AuthoredStateSchema is .strict() and hashAuthoredState hashes the snapshot as captured. A required-but-empty enablement field would change the hash of every authored state already on disk and manufacture a spurious revision on the next prepare. It must be optional and deleted when its last entry goes, and note the DO-NOT-TOUCH rule: data/linear.app/release-projects/flowpilot-wr27 has no revisions/ directory and smoke:revision 27A.23 asserts that.
